title: Backlog: deferred gauntlet follow-ups and stage attribution
objective: Persist the follow-ups deferred during the gauntlet rollout (FJ-043) so they survive session handoffs: design §13 batch notes, the report-retention policy promised by .agent/README.md, fail-closed selftest scenario gaps, hardening minors from T4-T9 reviews, repository hygiene, and the per-stage attribution spec gap (stage artifacts record no author).
acceptance: design §13 batch note records the approved wording tensions: []-omission vs §6.2 letter, pending vs in-progress vs §8.3
report-retention policy documented where .agent/README.md promises it, covering the untracked .agent/reports volume
stage attribution (per-stage author on stage artifacts) resolved only via a design/spec amendment first; the spec-gap is recorded below and no schema field is invented before it
fail-closed scenario gaps closed: PyYAML-absent, missing role pack, due/pending e2e assertion, scope-mismatch exemption, exempted+fail coexistence, non-list verificationCommands guards
hardening minors triaged: T7/T8/agent-context named minors addressed or explicitly rejected in notes; T4-T6 minors whose details were lost to session compaction are re-reviewed or dropped by decision
./scripts/verify-candidate and ./scripts/selftest still exit 0 after each change
nonGoals: no change to .agent/schema or public contracts before the design/spec amendment for attribution
no weakening of existing tests or gates to accommodate backlog items

blockers.description: Per-stage attribution (author/actor on stage-artifact headers) is defined neither in the specification nor in the gauntlet design (schema has stage, task, fingerprints, gitHead, generatedAt only). Requires a design/spec amendment before any schema change.

nextAction: triage the acceptance bullets when picked up; start attribution with a design/spec amendment, never a schema edit
notes: Umbrella backlog carried out of the FJ-043 close-out session; sub-items may be split into their own work items when picked up.
